title: Second largest distinct value
problem: Given an integer array, return the second largest DISTINCT value. If fewer than two distinct values exist, return Integer.MIN_VALUE.

frame.requirement: Says the input is an integer array
Says the output is a single integer
Notes that duplicates collapse — 'distinct' is doing work here
States what happens with fewer than two distinct values

plan.requirement: Proposes a single pass rather than sorting
States linear time and constant space

prompt.requirement: Says distinct, not just second largest
Names the edge cases to handle
Asks for or states the complexity

review.requirement: Spots that a duplicated maximum must not count as the runner-up
Spots that initialising trackers to 0 breaks all-negative input

reviewDecoys.requirement: Claims a memory leak, in a garbage-collected language

modelPromptExample:
Write a Java method `int secondLargest(int[] nums)` that returns the second largest DISTINCT value in the array.

Input: an int array, length 0 to 100000. Values may be negative and may repeat.
Output: the second largest distinct value, or Integer.MIN_VALUE when there are fewer than two distinct values.

Requirements:
- Handle these edge cases: empty array, single element, all elements equal, a duplicated maximum, and all-negative values.
- Target O(n) time and O(1) extra space. Do not sort.

Also state the time and space complexity.

Read n from stdin, then n integers, and print the result.

title: First non-repeating character
problem: Given a line of lowercase text, print the first character that appears exactly once. If every character repeats, print the word none.

frame.requirement: Says the input is a line of text
Says the output is one character or a word
States what to print when nothing is unique
Notes that FIRST means original order, not alphabetical

plan.requirement: Counts first, then scans in order
Uses a frequency map or a 26-slot array

prompt.requirement: Asks for or states the complexity

review.requirement: Checks it returns the FIRST such character, not any
Checks the all-repeating case prints none
Checks how non-letters or spaces are treated

reviewDecoys.requirement: Claims a stack overflow in an iterative solution

modelPromptExample:
Write a Java program that reads one line from stdin and prints the first character that appears exactly once in it.

Input: a single line, lowercase letters, possibly empty, up to 100000 characters.
Output: that one character on its own line, or the word none if every character repeats.

Requirements:
- First means earliest in the original order, not alphabetically smallest.
- Handle these edge cases: an empty line, a line where all characters repeat, and a single-character line.
- Target O(n) time using a frequency count.

Also state the complexity.
